patterns.exampleEnglish: If I had gone, I would have drunk the coffee.
patterns.grammarNote: لَوْ is a SECOND word for 'if', contrasted with إِذَا (level 57): إِذَا introduces a real or likely condition ('if/when I go...'), while لَوْ introduces a hypothetical or counterfactual one ('if I had gone...' — implying you didn't). Like إِذَا, لَوْ pairs with a past-tense verb, reusing your existing pool (level 22's ذَهَبْتُ, level 29's شَرِبْتُ) rather than minting new forms. The result clause often takes a لَـ prefix (لَشَرِبْتُ, 'I would have drunk') marking it as the hypothetical's consequence — لَـ attaches directly with no space, exactly like the other one-letter prefixes you already know (سَـ، بِ، وَ، كَـ).

exercises.prompt: Arrange the tiles to say 'If I had gone, I would have drunk the coffee.'
